import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the violin plot to visualize the distribution of camera prices across different sensor types
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.violinplot(
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    data=df,
    palette='viridis',
    inner='quartile', # Shows quartiles (median, 25th, 75th percentiles) inside the violins
    linewidth=1.0
)

# Add informative title and labels
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Price by Sensor Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if sensor type names are long
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Enhance layout
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
